[[Great Britain and Northern Ireland Olympic Team|'''Great Britain''']] competed '''at the [[2008 Summer Olympics]]''' in [[Beijing]], China.<ref name="BOA_TeamGB">{{cite web |url=http://www.olympics.org.uk/contentpage.aspx?page=127 |title=Team GB |access-date=21 August 2008 |work=British Olympic Association |archive-date=8 August 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080808021205/http://www.olympics.org.uk/contentpage.aspx?page=127 |url-status=dead }}</ref> The [[United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland|United Kingdom]] was represented by the [[British Olympic Association]] (BOA), one of only five [[National Olympic Committee]]s to have competed in every modern [[Summer Olympic Games]] since [[1896 Summer Olympics|the inaugural event in 1896]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uksport.gov.uk/about-us/who-we-work-with/british-olympic-association |title=British Olympic Association |quote=Great Britain is one of only five countries to have been represented at each summer Olympic Games since 1896 |website=[[UK Sport]] |access-date=21 May 2025 |archive-date=15 March 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250315105722/https://www.uksport.gov.uk/about-us/who-we-work-with/british-olympic-association |url-status=live }}</ref> The team of athletes selected to compete for the UK was officially known as [[Team GB]]; the delegation of 549 consisted of 313 competitors (169 men and 144 women) accompanied by 236 officials.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.olympics.org.uk/documents/downloads/section4.pdf |title=Team GB Beijing 2008 Handbook, Part 4: Team GB Biographies |work=British Olympic Association |access-date=21 May 2025 |archive-date=16 February 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100216131644/http://www.olympics.org.uk/documents/downloads/section4.pdf |url-status=dead |page=6 }}</ref> The team incorporated athletes from the whole of the UK, including [[Northern Ireland]] (whose citizens may be selected to represent either Great Britain or [[Ireland at the Olympics|Ireland]] at the Olympics if they have elected to hold [[Irish citizenship]]).<ref>{{cite web|title=Full text of the constitution |publisher=Department of the Taoiseach |url=http://www.taoiseach.gov.ie/attached_files/Pdf%20files/Constitution%20of%20Ireland.pdf |access-date=17 September 2008 |url-status=dead |archive-url=http://webarchive.loc.gov/all/20050415121010/http://www.taoiseach.gov.ie/attached_files/Pdf%20files/Constitution%20of%20Ireland.pdf |archive-date=15 April 2005 }}</ref> Additionally, three of the [[British Overseas Territories]] compete separately from Britain in Olympic competition, namely [[Bermuda at the 2008 Summer Olympics|Bermuda]], the [[British Virgin Islands at the 2008 Summer Olympics|British Virgin Islands]] and the [[Cayman Islands at the 2008 Summer Olympics|Cayman Islands]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://bvi.org.uk/we-are-the-british-overseas-territories-celebrating-the-achievements-of-the-british-overseas-territories-in-the-olympic-games/ |title=We Are the British Overseas Territories! Celebrating the Achievements of the British Overseas Territories in the Olympic Games. |website=bvi.org.uk |access-date=21 April 2025 |archive-date=14 January 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250114005213/https://bvi.org.uk/we-are-the-british-overseas-territories-celebrating-the-achievements-of-the-british-overseas-territories-in-the-olympic-games/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

Great Britain's Olympic medal performance in 2008 was its best in a century; at the close of the Games, the overall medal count of 47 was the second highest ever achieved by Team GB. The total number of gold medals was the highest since the [[1908 Summer Olympics]], which Britain hosted in London. Following the retesting of samples in 2016 in connection with the [[Russian doping scandal]], disqualifications led to four further bronze medals being awarded to Great Britain in athletics: both the men's and women's {{nowrap|4 × 400 metres}} relay teams were officially upgraded to bronze; [[Kelly Sotherton]] received her second reallocated bronze medal, in the women's heptathlon event (having also been part of the women's relay team); and [[Goldie Sayers]] was awarded the bronze medal for the women's javelin throw event. These four additional medals retrospectively increased Team GB's total medal count to 51.

Great Britain finished fourth overall in the Olympic medal table, a target that had previously been set by [[UK Sport]] (the public body responsible for distributing funding to elite sport) for the [[2012 Summer Olympics]], which was hosted by the UK in London; after Team GB's success in 2008, UK Sport considered whether to target third place for 2012.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/olympic_games/london_2012/7579901.stm |title=Britain may aim for third in 2012 |access-date=29 May 2008 |work=[[BBC Sport]] |date=25 August 2008 |first=James |last=Munro |archive-date=7 February 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220207092945/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/olympic_games/london_2012/7579901.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> Team GB finished top of the medal tables in [[Cycling at the 2008 Summer Olympics#Medal table|cycling]], [[Sailing at the 2008 Summer Olympics#Medal table|sailing]] and [[Rowing at the 2008 Summer Olympics#Medal table|rowing]], and third in [[Swimming at the 2008 Summer Olympics#Medal table|swimming]]. The highest number of medals was won in [[Cycling at the 2008 Summer Olympics|cycling]], with a total of 14, eight of which were gold. Britain also won gold medals in [[Sailing at the 2008 Summer Olympics|sailing]], [[Rowing at the 2008 Summer Olympics|rowing]], [[Swimming at the 2008 Summer Olympics|swimming]], [[Athletics at the 2008 Summer Olympics|athletics]], [[Canoeing at the 2008 Summer Olympics|canoeing]] and [[Boxing at the 2008 Summer Olympics|boxing]]. There were several outstanding individual achievements: cyclist [[Chris Hoy]] was the first Briton in 100 years to win three gold medals at a single Olympic Games; [[Rebecca Adlington]]'s double Olympic gold was the best performance by a British swimmer for a century; [[Ben Ainslie]] won a gold medal for the third successive Games to become the most decorated British Olympic sailor of all time; [[Rebecca Romero]] became the first British woman to win a medal in two different Olympic sports, winning a rowing silver in [[2004 Summer Olympics|2004]] and a cycling gold in 2008; and [[Louis Smith (gymnast)|Louis Smith]] was the first Briton to win an individual gymnastics medal since [[1908 Summer Olympics|1908]].

As the UK was to host the 2012 Summer Olympics in London, the [[2008 Summer Olympics closing ceremony|closing ceremony]] on 24&nbsp;August included a London 2012 handover performance<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cctv.com/english/special/closingceremony/20080824/110944.shtml |title=London handover performance |website=[[CCTV.com]] |date=24 August 2008 |access-date=22 May 2025 |archive-date=6 August 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240806135050/https://www.cctv.com/english/special/closingceremony/20080824/110944.shtml |url-status=live }}</ref> featuring football star [[David Beckham]], singer [[Leona Lewis]] and musician [[Jimmy Page]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2008/aug/24/olympics20083 |title=Olympics: Beijing brings Games to a close in dramatic fashion |last=Williams |first=Richard |work=The Guardian |location=Beijing |date=24 August 2008 |access-date=22 May 2025 |archive-date=26 April 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210426232807/https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2008/aug/24/olympics20083 |url-status=live }}</ref> as well as London mayor [[Boris Johnson]] and a London [[double-decker bus]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mercurynews.com/2008/08/24/olympics-closing-ceremony-is-fittingly-grand/ |title=Olympics’ closing ceremony is, fittingly, grand |last=Almond |first=Elliott |work=[[The Mercury News]] |location=Beijing |date=14 August 2016 |orig-date=24 August 2008 |access-date=22 May 2025 |archive-date=27 April 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170427140236/https://www.mercurynews.com/2008/08/24/olympics-closing-ceremony-is-fittingly-grand/ |url-status=live }}</ref>
{{TOC limit}}

==Medals==
{{further|2008 Summer Olympics medal table}}

At the close of the Games, Great Britain had won a total of 47 medals, 19 of which were gold.<ref name="Guardian original medal count" /> This was the second highest medal haul ever achieved by Team GB and the highest in a century,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/olympics/7568116.stm |title=GB Olympians power to new heights |work=BBC Sport |date=19 August 2008 |access-date=29 May 2025 |archive-date=30 March 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220330210955/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/olympics/7568116.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> representing the team's best Olympic performance since the [[1908 Summer Olympics]], which Britain hosted in London.<ref name="BBC_15736977">{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/olympics/15736977 |title=GB on target to beat medal haul from Beijing Olympics at London 2012 |work=BBC Sport |date=15 November 2011 |access-date=29 May 2025 |archive-date=14 June 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210614070434/https://www.bbc.com/sport/olympics/15736977 |url-status=live }}</ref> Great Britain finished fourth overall in the [[2008 Summer Olympics medal table|Olympics medal table]], behind [[China at the 2008 Summer Olympics|China]], [[United States at the 2008 Summer Olympics|United States]] and [[Russia at the 2008 Summer Olympics|Russia]].<ref name="Guardian original medal count" /><ref name="BBC_15736977" />

The following British competitors won medals at the Games (in August 2008).<ref>{{cite web |title=Medallists GBR – Great Britain |website=Beijing 2008 official website |url=http://results.beijing2008.cn/WRM/ENG/INF/GL/92A/GBR_T.shtml |access-date=17 September 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090303152247/http://results.beijing2008.cn/WRM/ENG/INF/GL/92A/GBR_T.shtml|archive-date=3 March 2009}}</ref> Note that the names of the Team GB medallists are shown '''in bold''' in the results tables given for each discipline in the sections below.

==Medal targets==
[[UK Sport]], which distributes [[National Lottery (United Kingdom)|National Lottery]] funding to elite sport, published its expectations for the Beijing Olympics in June 2008. The target medal count was set at 41 "potential" medals, with 35 of those identified as "expected" to be won, including 10 to 12 gold medals. Team GB's overall objective was to finish eighth in the medal table.<ref name="BBC GB target 35">{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/olympics/7485125.stm |work=BBC Sport |title=GB target 35 medals from Beijing |date=2 July 2008 |access-date=17 August 2008 |archive-date=17 January 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210117021756/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/olympics/7485125.stm |url-status=live }}</ref>

The gold medal expectation was exceeded on 19&nbsp;August when [[Paul Goodison]] earned Britain's 13th gold medal in the [[Sailing at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Men's Laser class|men's Laser class]] sailing event. The expectation of 35 medals was passed on 20&nbsp;August when Team GB claimed their 36th medal&nbsp;– a bronze in the [[Sailing at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Women's sailboard|women's RS:X]] sailing event, won by [[Bryony Shaw]]. The overall medal target of 41 was achieved when canoeist [[Tim Brabants]] took gold in the [[Canoeing at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Men's K-1 1000 metres|men's 1000&nbsp;m&nbsp;K-1]] canoeing event, claiming Britain's 41st physical medal (three further medals were guaranteed in boxing at the time),<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/olympics/canoeing/7576129.stm|title=Brabants wins Britain's 18th gold|access-date=22 August 2008 |work=BBC Sport |date=22 August 2008}}</ref> and the target was exceeded when [[Heather Fell]] secured the 42nd medal, a silver, in the [[Modern pentathlon at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Women's|women's modern pentathlon]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/olympics/modern_pentathlon/7576185.stm|title=Schoneborn pips GB's Fell to gold|access-date=22 August 2008 |work=BBC Sport |date=22 August 2008}}</ref>

Not all of the medals claimed had been identified and included in the target medal count; although Team GB fell short of targets in some disciplines, they exceeded targets in others. For example, the cycling target of six medals was met twice over on 19&nbsp;August when [[Victoria Pendleton]] won Britain's 12th cycling medal, a gold in the [[Cycling at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Women's sprint|women's sprint]] event.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/olympics/cycling/7569791.stm|title=Briton Pendleton wins sprint gold|access-date=19 August 2008 |work=BBC Sport |date=19 August 2008}}</ref> A further two medals were already guaranteed at this stage in the men's individual sprint: [[Chris Hoy]] and [[Jason Kenny]] subsequently won gold and silver, respectively.<ref name="Third Hoy gold"/> Altogether, Team GB won seven of the ten gold medals available in the track cycling events at the [[Laoshan Velodrome|velodrome]].<ref name="BBC 17039417">{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cycling/17039417 |title=London 2012: Britain's Beijing velodrome heroes – where are they now? |last=Williams |first=Ollie |work=BBC Sport |date=15 February 2012 |access-date=9 April 2025 |archive-date=3 August 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210803203343/https://www.bbc.com/sport/cycling/17039417 |url-status=live }}</ref> The swimmers also doubled their targeted medal count when [[David Davies (swimmer)|David Davies]] won the team's sixth swimming medal&nbsp;– a silver in the [[Swimming at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Men's marathon 10 kilometre|men's 10&nbsp;km open water marathon]] on 21&nbsp;August.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/olympics/swimming/7573725.stm|title=Battling Davies lands 10km silver|access-date=21 August 2008 |work=BBC Sport |date=21 August 2008}}</ref> Despite the men's and women's archery teams having placed second and third, respectively, at the 2007 world championships,<ref name="ArcheryLeipzig" /> the British archers won neither of their targeted medals, leading to criticism of the tactics used by head coach Peter Suk from members of the team.<ref>{{cite news |title=Wills criticises coach after exit |work=BBC Sport |date=15 August 2008 |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/olympics/archery/7562457.stm |access-date=19 September 2008}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Archery boss keen to hear critics |last=Scrivener |first=Peter |work=BBC Sport |date=4 September 2008 |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/olympics/archery/7598635.stm |access-date=19 September 2008}}</ref>

[[File:CyclingTeamPursuitBeijing2008.jpg|thumb|upright=1.4|Medal ceremony for the [[Cycling at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Men's team pursuit|men's team pursuit]] event, [[Laoshan Velodrome]], 18 August 2008]]

==Archery==
{{See also|Archery at the 2008 Summer Olympics}}
At the [[2007 World Outdoor Target Championships]], Great Britain's men's team placed second and its women's team placed third.<ref name="ArcheryLeipzig">{{cite web |url=http://www.archery.org/UserFiles/Document/Results/Results/07_WC_Outdoor_Leipzig/ECOMPR.pdf |title=2007 World Outdoor Target Championship Results |access-date=9 August 2008 |website=archery.org |page=2 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120211153158/http://www.archery.org/UserFiles/Document/Results/Results/07_WC_Outdoor_Leipzig/ECOMPR.pdf |archive-date=11 February 2012 |url-status=dead}}</ref> This qualified the nation to send the maximum quota of three men and three women to the 2008 Olympics.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.tntsports.co.uk/archery/olympics/2008/team-gbs-archers_sto1530041/story.shtml |title=Team GBs archers |website=TNT Sports |date=15 July 2008 |access-date=2 April 2025}}</ref>

==Athletics==
[[File:OhuruoguBeijing.jpg|thumb|[[Christine Ohuruogu]] after winning the [[Athletics at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Women's 400 metres|women's 400 metres]] event<ref name="TeamGB.com Ohuruogu gold">{{cite web|url=https://www.teamgb.com/video/christine-ohuruogu-clinches-400m-gold/2ALF1i7swqL32wanIW0KYz |title=Christine Ohuruogu Clinches 400m Gold |website=TeamGB.com |date=17 May 2020 |access-date=13 April 2025 |archive-date=16 September 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210916063810/https://www.teamgb.com/video/christine-ohuruogu-clinches-400m-gold/2ALF1i7swqL32wanIW0KYz |url-status=live }}</ref>]]
{{See also|Athletics at the 2008 Summer Olympics}}
The initial squad was selected for the British team on 14 July; however, the final team was not confirmed until the outcome of a court case involving [[Dwain Chambers]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/olympics/athletics/7504963.stm |title=Sprinters in limbo as squad named |access-date=9 August 2008 |work=[[BBC Sport]] |date=14 July 2008 |archive-date=3 June 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220603215459/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/olympics/athletics/7504963.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> Under [[British Olympic Association|BOA]] rules, Chambers had been banned from future Games after testing positive for the steroid THG in 2003; his appeal to overturn the ban (on the grounds that it was an unfair "restraint of trade") failed, and he was omitted from the squad.<ref>{{cite news |title=Chambers loses Olympic ban case |work=BBC Sport |date=18 July 2008 |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/olympics/athletics/7503792.stm |access-date=9 August 2008 |archive-date=27 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211127182648/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/olympics/athletics/7503792.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> The athletics team included former Olympic medal winners [[Marlon Devonish]] and [[Kelly Sotherton]], as well as former Olympic individual finalists [[Joanne Pavey]], [[Paula Radcliffe]], [[Helen Clitheroe]] and [[Tasha Danvers]]. Women's [[World records in athletics|marathon world record]] holder [[Paula Radcliffe]] faced a battle to be fit for the Games because of a [[stress fracture]] in her left thigh.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/olympics/athletics/7500721.stm |title=Radcliffe faces race against time |access-date=9 August 2008 |work=BBC Sport |date=14 July 2008 |archive-date=22 January 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160122162727/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/olympics/athletics/7500721.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> She was eventually fit enough to start the race but struggled to complete the distance and finished in 23rd position.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/othersports/olympics/2572474/Paula-Radcliffes-marathon-bid-ends-in-tears---Beijing-Olympics-2008.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080820013316/http://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/othersports/olympics/2572474/Paula-Radcliffes-marathon-bid-ends-in-tears---Beijing-Olympics-2008.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=20 August 2008 |title=Paula Radcliffe's marathon bid ends in tears |access-date=17 September 2008 |work=The Telegraph |date=17 August 2008 }}</ref>

Team GB won four medals in athletics: one gold, two silver and one bronze. [[UK Athletics]] performance director Dave Collins was forced to stand down from his post after the Games, due in part to the team's failure to meet the [[UK Sport]] target of winning five medals.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.insidethegames.biz/articles/1044412/three-belated-beijing-2008-bronze-medals-leave-sacked-uk-athletics-performance-director-collins-feeling-robbed |title=Three belated Beijing 2008 bronze medals leave sacked UK Athletics performance director Collins feeling robbed |last=Rowbottom |first=Mike |website=[[insidethegames.biz]] |date=8 December 2016 |access-date=7 May 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230604144550/https://www.insidethegames.biz/articles/1044412/three-belated-beijing-2008-bronze-medals-leave-sacked-uk-athletics-performance-director-collins-feeling-robbed |archive-date=4 June 2023 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="BBC GB target 35" /><ref>{{cite news |title=Collins leaves UK Athletics post |work=BBC Sport |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/athletics/7591761.stm |date=1 September 2008 |access-date=17 September 2008 |archive-date=9 May 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210509071143/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/athletics/7591761.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> Subsequently, a series of retests ordered in the wake of the [[Russian doping scandal]] in 2015 and 2016 found that Britain had been deprived of medals in a further four events by athletes later confirmed to have committed doping violations at the 2008 Games. In September 2016, javelin thrower [[Goldie Sayers]] and the entire [[Athletics at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Men's 4 × 400 metres relay|Men's 4 × 400 metres relay team]] were upgraded to bronze after confirmation that their Russian rivals had been retrospectively stripped of their medals for failing retests for banned substances.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/athletics/2016/05/25/britons-poised-for-olympic-glory-eight-years-late/ |title=Britons poised for Olympic glory eight years late |last=Bloom |first=Ben |work=The Telegraph |date=25 May 2016 |access-date=7 May 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210121000732/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/athletics/2016/05/25/britons-poised-for-olympic-glory-eight-years-late/ |archive-date=21 January 2021 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2016/sep/13/four-russian-athletes-sanctioned-ioc-failed-drugs-tests |title=Goldie Sayers and GB's 4x400m relay team upgraded to 2008 bronze |agency=Press Association |work=The Guardian |date=13 September 2016 |access-date=7 May 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220920133418/https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2016/sep/13/four-russian-athletes-sanctioned-ioc-failed-drugs-tests |archive-date=20 September 2022 |url-status=live }}</ref> Two further disqualifications resulting from the retest of doping samples led to the [[Athletics at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Women's 4 × 400 metres relay|Women's 4 × 400 metres relay team]] being upgraded from fifth place to bronze medal position.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/athletics/44891374 |title=Great Britain's 2008 4x400m women's relay team to get Olympic bronzes on Saturday |work=BBC Sport |date=19 July 2018 |access-date=7 May 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181127224013/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/athletics/44891374 |archive-date=27 November 2018 |url-status=live }}</ref> In September 2018, [[Kelly Sotherton]] was awarded a retrospective individual bronze medal in the women's heptathlon (her second reallocated bronze, as she was also part of the upgraded relay team)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympics.com/en/news/kelly-sotherton-receives-beijing-2008-heptathlon-bronze-a-decade-late |title=Kelly Sotherton receives Beijing 2008 heptathlon bronze a decade late |website=Olympics.com |date=14 September 2018 |access-date=7 May 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240816080619/https://www.olympics.com/en/news/kelly-sotherton-receives-beijing-2008-heptathlon-bronze-a-decade-late |archive-date=16 August 2024 |url-status=live }}</ref>—having originally placed fifth, she had been promoted to fourth position a few days after the event when Ukraine's [[Liudmyla Blonska]] was immediately stripped of her silver medal for failing a drugs test.<ref name="BBC 7571867">{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/olympics/athletics/7571867.stm |title=Blonska stripped of silver medal |work=BBC Sport |date=22 August 2008 |access-date=7 May 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200803164740/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/olympics/athletics/7571867.stm |archive-date=3 August 2020 |url-status=live }}</ref> <!--When these four medals were redistributed, Great Britain's 2008 athletics total of eight medals was its most successful since the second world war.{{cn|date=May 2025}}-->

<small><nowiki>*</nowiki> The athlete who finished in second place, [[Lyudmila Blonska]] of [[Ukraine at the 2008 Summer Olympics|Ukraine]], failed an initial drugs test immediately after the event.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.thetimes.com/sport/athletics/article/kelly-sotherton-welcomes-heptathlete-blonskas-failed-drugs-test-jq65x69w70r |title=Kelly Sotherton welcomes heptathlete Blonska's failed drugs test |access-date=30 March 2025 |work=[[The Times]] |date=20 August 2008 |location=London |first1=Rick |last1=Broadbent |first2=Ashling |last2=O'Connor |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250330065856/https://www.thetimes.com/sport/athletics/article/kelly-sotherton-welcomes-heptathlete-blonskas-failed-drugs-test-jq65x69w70r |archive-date=30 March 2025 |url-status=live |url-access=subscription}}</ref> She was stripped of her silver medal on 22&nbsp;August 2008 when both her A and B samples tested positive for a banned substance,<ref name="BBC 7571867" /> and both British heptathletes were moved up a position.</small><!--Note: Hollman ended up in 30th position when Sotherton got her bronze medal ten years later. -->

==Badminton==
{{See also|Badminton at the 2008 Summer Olympics}}
Six British badminton players went to the Games,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.badmintonengland.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2021/08/Facts-and-Records-as-at-May-2021.pdf |title=Badminton England Facts and Records |work=[[Badminton England]] |date=May 2021 |access-date=6 April 2025 |page=3 |archive-date=25 February 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240225022331/https://www.badmintonengland.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2021/08/Facts-and-Records-as-at-May-2021.pdf |url-status=live }}</ref> competing in four of the five badminton events. They did not win any medals, thus failing to reach the [[#Targets|one medal target]] set by [[UK Sport]].<ref name="BBC GB target 35" /> The [[Badminton at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Mixed doubles|mixed doubles]] pairing of [[Gail Emms]] and [[Nathan Robertson]], who won silver in the [[Badminton at the 2004 Summer Olympics – Mixed doubles|2004 tournament]], progressed furthest amongst the British athletes, reaching the quarterfinals.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2008/aug/14/olympicgames.badminton |title=Olympics: Curtain falls on Emms' career as mixed doubles are denied |last=Bull |first=Andy |work=The Guardian |orig-date=14 August 2008 |date=15 August 2008 |access-date=6 April 2025 |archive-date=1 March 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140301182355/https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2008/aug/14/olympicgames.badminton |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Boxing==
{{See also|Boxing at the 2008 Summer Olympics}}
Great Britain qualified eight entrants for the boxing competition.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/olympics/2466261/Beijing-Olympics-British-Boxings-2008-class.html |title=Beijing Olympics: British Boxing's 2008 class |last=Davies |first=Gareth A. |work=The Telegraph |date=7 August 2008 |access-date=6 April 2025 |archive-date=12 May 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230512153045/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/olympics/2466261/Beijing-Olympics-British-Boxings-2008-class.html |url-status=live }}</ref> [[David Price (boxer)|David Price]] and [[Tony Jeffries]] won bronze medals in the [[Boxing at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Super heavyweight|super heavyweight]] and [[Boxing at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Light heavyweight|light heavyweight]] divisions, respectively,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/boxing/58818452 |title=David Price: British heavyweight retires from boxing aged 38 |work=BBC Sport |date=6 October 2021 |access-date=6 April 2025 |archive-date=6 October 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211006201442/https://www.bbc.com/sport/boxing/58818452 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="bleacher boxing">{{cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2605983-reviewing-the-progress-of-great-britains-boxers-from-the-2008-olympics |title=Reviewing the Progress of Great Britain's Boxers from the 2008 Olympics |last=Lancaster |first=Rob |website=[[Bleacher Report]] |date=3 June 2018 |access-date=6 April 2025 |archive-date=27 January 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160127181603/https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2605983-reviewing-the-progress-of-great-britains-boxers-from-the-2008-olympics |url-status=live }}</ref> and [[James DeGale]] won gold in the [[Boxing at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Middleweight|middleweight]] class.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2008/aug/23/olympics.boxing |title=Olympics: James DeGale wins gold for Britain in middleweight boxing |last=Ingle |first=Sean |work=The Guardian |date=23 August 2008 |access-date=6 April 2025 |archive-date=24 February 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190224051712/https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2008/aug/23/olympics.boxing |url-status=live }}</ref> This was the first time since [[Great Britain at the 1972 Summer Olympics|1972]] that Team GB had won more than one boxing medal in a single Olympic Games,<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2008/aug/19/olympics2008.olympicsboxing |title=Olympics: Guaranteed bronze for light-heavyweight Jeffries |access-date=19 August 2008 |work=[[The Guardian]] |date=19 August 2008 |location=London |first=Pete |last=Nichols |archive-date=27 November 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241127002247/https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2008/aug/19/olympics2008.olympicsboxing |url-status=live }}</ref> and it was Britain's best result in Olympic boxing since [[Great Britain at the 1956 Summer Olympics|1956]].<ref name="bleacher boxing" />

==Canoeing==
{{See also|Canoeing at the 2008 Summer Olympics}}
Seven competitors joined Team GB for the canoeing events, with three in the slalom and four in the flatwater sprint. [[Anna Hemmings]] and [[Jessica Walker]], in the K-2 kayaking pairs, were a late addition to the team after qualification complications with the Spanish team.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/olympics/canoeing/7514092.stm |title=Kayak pair finally named for GB |access-date=9 August 2008 |work=BBC Sport |date=18 July 2008 |archive-date=3 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230403224540/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/olympics/canoeing/7514092.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> Three medals were won, exceeding the target of two set by [[UK Sport]].<ref name="BBC GB target 35" /> Two of the medals were won by sprint kayaker [[Tim Brabants]], who had previously won a bronze at the [[Canoeing at the 2000 Summer Olympics|2000 Olympics]] in Sydney.<ref name="BBC GB target 35" />

==Cycling==
{{See also|Cycling at the 2008 Summer Olympics}}
[[File:Chris Hoy.jpg|thumb|upright=0.6|Triple gold medallist [[Chris Hoy]]<ref name="Guardian Hoy triple gold">{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2008/aug/20/chrishoy.olympicscycling |title=Olympics: Hoy makes history with Olympic treble |work=The Guardian |last=Williams |first=Richard |date=20 August 2008 |access-date=9 April 2025 |archive-date=9 April 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250409114437/https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2008/aug/20/chrishoy.olympicscycling |url-status=live }}</ref>]]
Team GB's cycling squad for Beijing totalled twenty-five entrants in the four disciplines.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2008/jul/09/olympicgames.cycling |title=Burke and Kenny named for Beijing as GB's Brailsford goes for youth |last=Fotheringham |first=William |work=The Guardian |date=9 July 2008 |access-date=25 May 2025 |archive-date=4 January 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160104020840/https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2008/jul/09/olympicgames.cycling |url-status=live }}</ref> Included were two [[Cycling at the 2004 Summer Olympics|reigning Olympic track cycling champions]], Chris Hoy and Bradley Wiggins, plus a further two medal winners from 2004, as well as several [[2008 UCI Track Cycling World Championships|reigning track world champions]]. Great Britain won a total of fourteen cycling medals (eight gold, four silver and two bronze)<ref name="BBC_15736977" /> to top the [[Cycling at the 2008 Summer Olympics#Medal table|cycling medal table]]. Britain's Olympic cycling team won the 2008 [[BBC Sports Team of the Year Award]]<ref name="BBC_SPOTY">{{cite press release|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/pressoffice/pressreleases/stories/2008/12_december/14/sports.shtml |title=Chris Hoy wins BBC 2008 Sports Personality of the Year |work=BBC Press Office |date=14 December 2008 |access-date=23 May 2025 |archive-date=11 December 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131211042654/https://www.bbc.co.uk/pressoffice/pressreleases/stories/2008/12_december/14/sports.shtml |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="Guardian_SPOTY">{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2008/dec/15/chris-hoy-bbc-sports-personality1 |title=Cyclist Chris Hoy wins BBC Sports Personality of the Year Award 2008 |last=Gibson |first=Owen |work=The Guardian |date=15 December 2008 |access-date=23 May 2025 |archive-date=14 May 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230514203338/https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2008/dec/15/chris-hoy-bbc-sports-personality1 |url-status=live }}</ref> and received a nomination for [[Laureus World Team of the Year]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.laureus.com/world-sports-awards/2009/laureus-world-team-of-the-year/great-britain-olympic-cycling-team |title=Great Britain Olympic Cycling Team {{!}} Laureus |website=Laureus.com |access-date=23 May 2025 |archive-date=22 January 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250122102001/https://www.laureus.com/world-sports-awards/2009/laureus-world-team-of-the-year/great-britain-olympic-cycling-team |url-status=live }}</ref>

On the track, [[Mark Cavendish]] was the only member of the squad of fourteen not to win at least one medal.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.cyclingnews.com/news/cavendish-i-dont-know-if-id-have-been-able-to-make-it-without-wiggins/ |title=Cavendish: I don't know if I'd have been able to make it without Wiggins |website=[[Cyclingnews.com]] |date=24 June 2016 |access-date=25 May 2025 |archive-date=22 September 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210922215001/https://www.cyclingnews.com/news/cavendish-i-dont-know-if-id-have-been-able-to-make-it-without-wiggins/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Chris Hoy became Scotland's most successful Olympic competitor ever,<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/olympics/cycling/7565356.stm|title=Hoy & Edgar claim gold and silver|access-date=17 August 2008 |work=[[BBC Sport]] |date=16 August 2008 |archive-date=15 March 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150315043946/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/olympics/cycling/7565356.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> and the first Briton to win three gold medals at a single Olympic Games since [[Henry Taylor (swimmer)|Henry Taylor]] in 1908.<ref name="Guardian Hoy triple gold" /><ref name="Third Hoy gold">{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/olympics/cycling/7569650.stm|title=Hoy clinches historic third gold|access-date=19 August 2008 |work=BBC Sport |date=19 August 2008 |archive-date=15 March 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150315043730/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/olympics/cycling/7569650.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> Hoy was named the 2008 [[BBC Sports Personality of the Year Award|BBC Sports Personality of the Year]],<ref name="BBC_SPOTY" /><ref name="Guardian_SPOTY" /> and his medal success resulted in the [[Sir Chris Hoy Velodrome|velodrome]] for the [[2014 Commonwealth Games]] in Glasgow being named in his honour.<ref>{{cite news |title=Velodrome honour for golden Hoy |work=BBC News |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/scotland/7570483.stm |access-date=19 August 2008 |date=19 August 2008 |archive-date=15 March 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150315043930/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/scotland/7570483.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> Rebecca Romero became the first British woman to [[List of multiple Olympic medalists#Athletes with medals in different disciplines|win a medal in two different Olympic sports]] by following her silver medal in the [[Rowing at the 2004 Summer Olympics – Women's quadruple sculls|quadruple sculls]] rowing in 2004 with gold in the [[Cycling at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Women's individual pursuit|women's individual pursuit]].<ref name="BBC Romero">{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/olympics/cycling/7565385.stm|title=Romero beats GB team-mate to gold |access-date=17 August 2008 |work=BBC Sport |date=17 August 2008 |archive-date=22 January 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160122162727/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/olympics/cycling/7565385.stm |url-status=live }}</ref>

In the debut appearance of [[BMX at the Summer Olympics|BMX events at the Olympics]], world champion [[Shanaze Reade]] finished out of the medals after crashing out of the [[Cycling at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Women's BMX|women's final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.chinadaily.com.cn/olympics/2008-08/22/content_6961938_2.htm |title=Shanaze Reade falls in the BMX cycling race |work=[[China Daily]] |date=22 August 2008 |access-date=25 May 2025 |archive-date=18 June 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200618191049/https://www.chinadaily.com.cn/olympics/2008-08/22/content_6961938_2.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> Reade had been unbeaten all year and was the favourite to win the women's title.<ref>{{cite news |title=Reade crashes out of BMX medals |work=BBC Sport |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/olympics/cycling/7575946.stm |date=22 August 2008 |access-date=17 September 2008 |archive-date=22 January 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160122162727/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/olympics/cycling/7575946.stm |url-status=live }}</ref>

On the road, [[Nicole Cooke]] won the [[Cycling at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Women's individual road race|women's road race]], providing the first Olympic gold for an athlete from [[Sport in Wales|Wales]] since [[Richard Meade (equestrian)|Richard Meade]] in [[Equestrian events at the 1972 Summer Olympics|1972]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/wales/7552351.stm |title=Cyclist takes first Olympic gold |access-date=25 May 2025 |work=BBC News |date=10 August 2008 |archive-date=11 August 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080811012351/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/wales/7552351.stm |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Track===

==Diving==
{{See also|Diving at the 2008 Summer Olympics}}
Team GB entered a total of ten divers (five men and five women) into the individual and synchronised diving events.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://news.xinhuanet.com/english/2008-07/30/content_8856521.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121023081103/http://news.xinhuanet.com/english/2008-07/30/content_8856521.htm |url-status=dead |archive-date=23 October 2012 |title=British divers feel no pressure from dominant China |access-date=9 August 2008 |website=[[Xinhuanet.com]] |agency=[[Xinhua News Agency]] |date=30 July 2008 }}</ref> The diving team included 14-year-old [[Tom Daley (diver)|Tom Daley]], the [[2008 European Aquatics Championships|2008 European]] Men's 10-metre platform champion and one of the youngest athletes ever to compete for Great Britain at the Summer Olympics.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/olympics/diving/7518019.stm |title=Brits to watch: Tom Daley |access-date=17 September 2008 |work=BBC Sport |date=4 August 2008 |archive-date=22 April 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210422184815/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/olympics/diving/7518019.stm |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Equestrian==
{{See also|Equestrian at the 2008 Summer Olympics}}
Twelve entrants competed for Team GB in the three equestrian disciplines, which took place in [[Hong Kong]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympics.com/ioc/news/beijing-2008-equestrian-events-moved-to-hong-kong |title=Beijing 2008: equestrian events moved to Hong Kong |website=Olympics.com |date=7 July 2005 |access-date=5 April 2025 |archive-date=4 July 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220704004808/https://www.olympics.com/ioc/news/beijing-2008-equestrian-events-moved-to-hong-kong |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Zara Phillips]], the reigning [[Eventing World Championship|world eventing champion]] and granddaughter of Queen [[Elizabeth II]], was originally included in the squad but had to withdraw when her horse [[Toytown (horse)|Toytown]] sustained an injury during training; Phillips missed out on her second successive Olympics, having withdrawn from the [[2004 Summer Olympics|2004 Games]] for the same reason.<ref>{{cite news| title=Phillips out of GB Olympic team |work=BBC Sport |date=11 June 2008 |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/olympics/equestrian/7448590.stm |access-date=17 September 2008 |archive-date=10 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240410202956/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/olympics/equestrian/7448590.stm |url-status=live }}</ref>

[[Kristina Cook]] won an [[Equestrian at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Individual eventing|individual eventing]] bronze medal, and Britain also won bronze in the [[Equestrian at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Team eventing|three-day team event]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2008/aug/12/olympics2008.olympicsequestrian1 |title=Olympics: Three-day eventers take bronze for Great Britain as Cook adds individual third |last=Bierley |first=Steve |work=The Guardian |date=12 August 2008 |access-date=5 April 2025 |archive-date=22 August 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160822002254/https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2008/aug/12/olympics2008.olympicsequestrian1 |url-status=live }}</ref>

<small><nowiki>*</nowiki> Reserve rider Nick Skelton was added to the show jumping team event as a substitute for Michael Whitaker who had withdrawn from the competition.<ref name="BBC equestrian 7558349" /></small>

<small><nowiki>**</nowiki> On 21 August, four horses from [[Brazil at the 2008 Summer Olympics|Brazil]], [[Germany at the 2008 Summer Olympics|Germany]], [[Ireland at the 2008 Summer Olympics|Ireland]] and [[Norway at the 2008 Summer Olympics|Norway]] tested positive for a banned substance.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/olympics/equestrian/7574220.stm |title= Olympic horses fail drugs tests |access-date=21 August 2008 |work=BBC Sport |date=21 August 2008 |archive-date=24 February 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230224032055/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/olympics/equestrian/7574220.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> The riders were subsequently disqualified from the [[Equestrian at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Individual jumping|individual competition]] and if the B samples test positive then Brazil, Germany and Norway will be disqualified from the [[Equestrian at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Team jumping|team competition]] and Great Britain will move into 5th place.</small>

==Fencing==
{{See also|Fencing at the 2008 Summer Olympics}}
Great Britain qualified three fencers for the individual fencing events. Cambridge University student [[Alex O'Connell (fencer)|Alex O'Connell]] was the only fencer included in the original allocation for Team GB announced in May 2008.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/olympics/fencing/7369611.stm |title=O'Connell secures lone GB place |work=BBC Sport |date=8 May 2008 |access-date=4 April 2025 |archive-date=13 March 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220313223639/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/olympics/fencing/7369611.stm |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cam.ac.uk/news/cambridge-fencer-bound-for-beijing-olympics |title=Cambridge Fencer bound for Beijing Olympics |date=15 May 2008 |access-date=4 April 2025 |website=[[cam.ac.uk]] |archive-date=4 April 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250404100308/https://www.cam.ac.uk/news/cambridge-fencer-bound-for-beijing-olympics |url-status=live }}</ref> The other two British fencers were added through the re-allocation of places by the [[FIE]] (the governing body for Olympic fencing) following the withdrawal of entrants from other NOCs.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/olympics/fencing/7456865.stm |title=Kruse added to GB fencing squad |work=BBC Sport |date=26 June 2008 |access-date=4 April 2025 |archive-date=13 March 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220313223509/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/olympics/fencing/7456865.stm |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.olympics.org.uk/beijing2008/News.aspx?id=2499 |title=BOA Announce Another Fencer Selected for Team GB |access-date=9 August 2008 |publisher=[[British Olympic Association]] |date=17 July 2008 |archive-date=18 July 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080718230418/http://www.olympics.org.uk/beijing2008/news.aspx?id=2499 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Field hockey==
{{See also|Field hockey at the 2008 Summer Olympics}}

===Men's tournament===
{{See also|Field hockey at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament}}
The [[Great Britain men's national field hockey team|Great Britain men's team]] qualified for the men's Olympic field hockey tournament after a must-win game against [[India men's national field hockey team|India]] in the final of the [[Men's field hockey Qualifying Tournaments for the 2008 Summer Olympics#Qualifying 2|Olympic qualifying]] event.<ref>{{cite news |title=GB hockey men seal Beijing berth |work=BBC Sport |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/olympics/hockey/7286744.stm |date=9 March 2008 |access-date=17 September 2008 |archive-date=22 January 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160122162728/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/olympics/hockey/7286744.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> Great Britain was drawn in Group&nbsp;B of the Olympic tournament based on the [[FIH Men's World Ranking]]s on 17&nbsp;April 2008.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fih.hockey/general/news/fih-releases-pools-for-mens-olympic-hockey-tournament |title=FIH releases pools for Men's Olympic Hockey Tournament |work=[[International Hockey Federation]] |date=17 April 2008 |access-date=12 May 2025 |archive-date=12 May 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250512184902/https://www.fih.hockey/general/news/fih-releases-pools-for-mens-olympic-hockey-tournament |url-status=live }}</ref> Having finished third in their group, the team went on to finish fifth overall, beating [[South Korea men's national field hockey team|South Korea]] in the 5th/6th place classification match.<ref name="BBC hockey results">{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/olympics/hockey/latest_results/default.stm |title=Hockey results |work=BBC Sport |date=24 August 2008 |access-date=12 May 2025 |archive-date=21 July 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200721014054/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/olympics/hockey/latest_results/default.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Matt Daly]] was the team's top scorer in the tournament, with three goals.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympedia.org/results/260100/top_scorers/2 |title=Hockey, Men – Goals Ranking |website=[[Olympedia]] |access-date=12 May 2025 |archive-date=27 November 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241127121550/http://www.olympedia.org/results/260100/top_scorers/2 |url-status=live}}</ref>

===Women's tournament===
{{See also|Field hockey at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Women's tournament}}
The [[Great Britain women's national field hockey team|Great Britain women's team]] qualified for the women's Olympic field hockey tournament during the [[2007 Women's EuroHockey Nations Championship]].<ref name="FIH_squads" /> Great Britain was drawn in Group&nbsp;B of the Olympic tournament based on the [[FIH Women's World Ranking]]s on 5&nbsp;May 2008.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fihockey.org/vsite/vcontent/content/transnews/0,10869,1181-18543-19728-28355-285061--5039-layout169-19693-news-item,00.html |title=FIH releases pools for Women's Olympic Hockey Tournament |work=[[International Hockey Federation]] |date=5 May 2008 |access-date=12 May 2025 |archive-date=5 December 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231205052507/https://www.fihockey.org/vsite/vcontent/content/transnews/0,10869,1181-18543-19728-28355-285061--5039-layout169-19693-news-item,00.html |url-status=live }}</ref> Having finished third in their group, the team proceeded to the 5th/6th place classification match where they lost to [[Australia women's national field hockey team|Australia]].<ref name="BBC hockey results" /> [[Crista Cullen]] was the team's top scorer in the tournament, with three goals.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympedia.org/results/260144/top_scorers/2 |title=Hockey, Women – Goals Ranking |website=[[Olympedia]] |access-date=12 May 2025 |archive-date=19 February 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250219194203/https://www.olympedia.org/results/260144/top_scorers/2 |url-status=live}}</ref>

==Gymnastics==
{{See also|Gymnastics at the 2008 Summer Olympics}}
Team GB entered nine gymnasts into the [[Artistic gymnastics|artistic]] and [[Trampolining|trampoline]] events. On winning the bronze medal in the [[Gymnastics at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Men's pommel horse|men's pommel horse]] event,<ref name="TeamGB.com Smith bronze">{{cite web|url=https://www.teamgb.com/video/louis-smith-pommel-horse-bronze-beijing-2008/2y8WCKAygYvof8RaQdc900 |title=Louis Smith Pommel Horse Bronze |website=TeamGB.com |date=8 December 2020 |access-date=7 April 2025 |archive-date=16 September 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210916173229/https://www.teamgb.com/video/louis-smith-pommel-horse-bronze-beijing-2008/2y8WCKAygYvof8RaQdc900 |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Louis Smith (gymnast)|Louis Smith]] became the first Briton to win an individual [[Gymnastics at the Summer Olympics|gymnastics]] medal since [[Walter Tysall]] won silver in the [[Gymnastics at the 1908 Summer Olympics – Men's artistic individual all-around|men's all-around]] event in [[1908 Summer Olympics|1908]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/olympics/gymnastics/7566647.stm |title=Smith wins historic bronze for GB |access-date=17 August 2008 |work=BBC Sport |date=17 August 2008 |archive-date=6 March 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230306091826/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/olympics/gymnastics/7566647.stm |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2008/aug/17/olympics2008.olympicsgymnastics1 |title=Olympics: Smith's coach says bronze can lift gymnastics to greater heights |last=Kessel |first=Anna |work=The Guardian |date=18 August 2008 |access-date=4 April 2025 |archive-date=21 August 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220821081953/https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2008/aug/17/olympics2008.olympicsgymnastics1 |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Laura Jones (gymnast)|Laura Jones]] was originally selected to take part in the women's artistic team event but, because of a [[slipped disc]] in her back, she was replaced by the reserve gymnast [[Imogen Cairns]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/olympics/gymnastics/7514562.stm |title=Injured Jones out of Olympic team |access-date=9 August 2008 |work=BBC Sport |date=18 July 2008 |archive-date=20 January 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210120014419/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/olympics/gymnastics/7514562.stm |url-status=live }}</ref>

The result of the [[Gymnastics at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Women's uneven bars|uneven bars final]], in which Britain's Beth Tweddle placed 4th, was called into question after documents were found that seemed to say that Chinese gymnasts [[He Kexin]] and [[Yang Yilin]] were only 14, and therefore under the age required to compete, at the time of the Games. An investigation into their ages was launched by the IOC to determine whether it was necessary to disqualify them, thus Tweddle's standing could have been changed to 2nd, giving her a silver medal.<ref name="Times Aug 21">{{cite news |url=https://www.thetimes.com/travel/destinations/asia-travel/china/international-olympic-committee-launches-probe-into-he-kexins-age-xr98h7t8sp6 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250526132142/https://www.thetimes.com/travel/destinations/asia-travel/china/international-olympic-committee-launches-probe-into-he-kexins-age-xr98h7t8sp6 |url-status=live |archive-date=26 May 2025 |title=International Olympic Committee launches probe into He Kexin's age |access-date=26 May 2025 |url-access=subscription |work=[[The Times]] |date=22 August 2008 |location=London |first1=Tim |last1=Reid |first2=Jane |last2=MacArtney}}</ref> After a five-and-a-half-week investigation the Chinese athletes were cleared and the original results allowed to stand.<ref>{{cite web |title=2008 Chinese gymnasts cleared, but two from 2000 Games still eyed |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=1 October 2008 |url=https://www.espn.co.uk/olympics/gymnastics/news/story?id=3619325 |access-date=13 May 2025 |archive-date=20 January 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250120170419/https://www.espn.co.uk/olympics/gymnastics/news/story?id=3619325 |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Trampoline===
[[Claire Wright (gymnast)|Claire Wright]] was the only British competitor on the trampoline.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/olympics/gymnastics/7390444.stm |title=Team GB unveil lone trampolinist |work=BBC Sport |date=8 May 2008 |access-date=2 April 2025 |archive-date=4 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230404013822/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/olympics/gymnastics/7390444.stm |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Judo==
{{See also|Judo at the 2008 Summer Olympics}}
Team GB was represented in the judo events by seven [[judoka]] (four men and three women),<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ijf.org/competition/1698/judoka_nations?nation=gbr |title=Olympic Games Beijing 2008 / IJF.org {{!}} (37) Great Britain |work=[[International Judo Federation]] |access-date=13 May 2025 |archive-date=13 May 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250513183911/https://www.ijf.org/competition/1698/judoka_nations?nation=gbr |url-status=live }}</ref> including the 2005 world champion [[Craig Fallon]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/olympics/judo/7359587.stm |title=Fallon handed Olympic squad place |access-date=10 August 2008 |work=BBC Sport |date=22 April 2008 |archive-date=13 March 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220313224100/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/olympics/judo/7359587.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> None of the British entrants made it past the quarterfinal stages of the competition or through to the medal match of the [[repechage]], so the team failed to meet the two-medal target set by [[UK Sport]].<ref name="BBC GB target 35" />

==Modern pentathlon==
{{See also|Modern pentathlon at the 2008 Summer Olympics}}
Team GB sent the maximum allowance of four competitors for the [[modern pentathlon]] events in Beijing. For the first time since [[1996 Summer Olympics|1996]], the team had entrants in the men's competition.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.olympics.org.uk/beijing2008/news.aspx?id=2443 |title=BOA select additional Team GB Modern Pentathletes |access-date=10 August 2008 |publisher=[[British Olympic Association]] |date=2 July 2008 |archive-date=3 August 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080803215420/http://www.olympics.org.uk/beijing2008/News.aspx?id=2443 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Rowing==
{{See also|Rowing at the 2008 Summer Olympics}}
Great Britain was represented by 43 rowers in 12 boats,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.britishrowing.org/2008/06/biggest-gb-rowing-olympic-contingent-since-1992/ |title=Biggest GB rowing Olympic contingent since 1992 |website=BritishRowing.org |date=26 June 2008 |access-date=11 April 2025 |archive-date=14 January 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250114002037/https://www.britishrowing.org/2008/06/biggest-gb-rowing-olympic-contingent-since-1992/ |url-status=live }}</ref> the highest number since qualifying quotas were introduced for rowing after the [[1992 Summer Olympics]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/olympics/rowing/7509407.stm |title=Final GB rowers named after trial |access-date=10 August 2008 |work=BBC Sport |date=16 July 2008 |archive-date=4 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230404004645/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/olympics/rowing/7509407.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> Crews were fielded in 12 out of a possible 14 events,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.britishrowing.org/2008/08/and-so-it-begins/ |title=And so it begins |website=BritishRowing.org |date=7 August 2008 |access-date=11 April 2025 |archive-date=24 January 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250124095745/https://www.britishrowing.org/2008/08/and-so-it-begins/ |url-status=live }}</ref> making Team GB the fourth biggest team. Medals were won in six events,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.britishrowing.org/olympic-games/ |title=Olympic Games |website=BritishRowing.org |access-date=11 April 2025 |archive-date=5 December 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241205155419/https://www.britishrowing.org/olympic-games/ |url-status=live }}</ref> and Britain topped the [[Rowing at the 2008 Summer Olympics#Medal table|rowing medal table]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Medal Standings Rowing|website=Beijing 2008 official website |url=http://results.beijing2008.cn/WRM/ENG/INF/RO/C95/RO0000000.shtml|date=17 August 2008|access-date=17 September 2008|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080921000417/http://results.beijing2008.cn/WRM/ENG/INF/RO/C95/RO0000000.shtml|archive-date=21 September 2008}}</ref>
The medals won included gold in the [[Rowing at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Men's coxless four|coxless four]], for the third successive Games, and [[Zac Purchase]] and [[Mark Hunter (rower)|Mark Hunter]] winning Great Britain's first ever [[lightweight rowing]] Olympic medal in the [[Rowing at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Men's lightweight double sculls|men's lightweight double sculls]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/olympics/rowing/7566291.stm|title=GB duo win first lightweight gold|access-date=17 August 2008 |work=BBC Sport |date=17 August 2008 |archive-date=6 March 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230306121838/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/olympics/rowing/7566291.stm |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Sailing==
{{See also|Sailing at the 2008 Summer Olympics}}
Great Britain entered crews in all 11 sailing events at the Games.<ref name="Team GB athletes"/><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.olympics.org.uk/futuregamesqual.aspx?gt=s&ga=48#SA |title=British Olympic Association > Summer Games > Beijing 2008 > Qualification |access-date=10 August 2008 |publisher=[[British Olympic Association]] |archive-date=30 November 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101130184115/http://www.olympics.org.uk/futuregamesqual.aspx?gt=s&ga=48#SA |url-status=dead }}</ref> The team finished top of the [[Sailing at the 2008 Summer Olympics#Medal table|sailing medal table]], with six medals won,<ref>{{cite web|title=Medal Standings Sailing|website=Beijing 2008 official website|url=http://results.beijing2008.cn/WRM/ENG/INF/SA/C95/SA0000000.shtml|date=21 August 2008|access-date=17 September 2008|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080912221851/http://results.beijing2008.cn/WRM/ENG/INF/SA/C95/SA0000000.shtml|archive-date=12 September 2008}}</ref> thus exceeding the [[#Targets|target of four]] set by [[UK Sport]].<ref name="BBC GB target 35" /> [[Ben Ainslie]] won a gold medal for the third successive Games to become the most decorated British Olympic sailor of all time.<ref>{{cite news |title= Ainslie claims third Olympic gold |work=[[BBC Sport]] |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/olympics/sailing/7566239.stm |date=17 August 2008 |access-date=17 September 2008 |archive-date=11 September 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220911202052/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/olympics/sailing/7566239.stm |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Shooting==
{{See also|Shooting at the 2008 Summer Olympics}}
Great Britain qualified five entrants for the shooting competition, four in the [[shotgun]] events and one in the [[rifle]] events. Olympic gold medallist [[Richard Faulds]], who won the [[Shooting at the 2000 Summer Olympics – Men's double trap|Men's double trap in 2000]], progressed furthest amongst the British competitors, finishing in sixth place.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/olympics/shooting/7483321.stm |title=Faulds heading to fourth Olympics |work=BBC Sport |date=1 July 2008 |access-date=10 April 2025 |archive-date=13 March 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220313225109/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/olympics/shooting/7483321.stm |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.issf-sports.org/athletes/SHGBRM1603197701 |title=Richard Faulds in ISSF Athletes Database |website=issf-sports.org |access-date=10 April 2025 |archive-date=21 January 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250121012555/https://www.issf-sports.org/athletes/SHGBRM1603197701 |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Swimming==
{{See also|Swimming at the 2008 Summer Olympics}}
[[File:Rebecca adlington.png|thumb|upright=0.7|Double gold medallist [[Rebecca Adlington]]<ref name="Guardian Adlington_double" />]]
Thirty-seven athletes represented Team GB in the swimming events. Selection followed the [[2008 British Olympic Swimming Trials]] in Sheffield in April, with open water event swimmers selected after performance in the 2008 World Open Water Swimming Championships, in [[Seville]], Spain. In winning six medals (two gold, two silver and two bronze) the team bettered the [[#Targets|target]] of three medals set by [[UK Sport]].<ref name="BBC GB target 35" /> [[Rebecca Adlington]] was the most successful swimmer, winning two gold medals.<ref name="Guardian Adlington_double">{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2008/aug/16/olympics2008.olympicsaquatics3 |title=Olympics: Brilliant Adlington wins second gold of Games |last=Buckley |first=Will |work=The Guardian |date=16 August 2008 |access-date=12 April 2025 |archive-date=11 February 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210211084401/https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2008/aug/16/olympics2008.olympicsaquatics3 |url-status=live }}</ref> Her 400&nbsp;m freestyle success was Britain's first Olympic swimming title since [[Great Britain at the 1988 Summer Olympics|1988]], and the first swimming gold by a British woman since [[Great Britain at the 1960 Summer Olympics|1960]]. Her second gold, in the 800&nbsp;m freestyle, meant she also equalled the best performance by a British woman, from any sport, at the summer Olympics and was the best swimming performance by a Briton at the Olympics for 100 years.<ref name="BBC Adlington storms">{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/olympics/swimming/7564653.stm|title=Adlington storms to second gold |access-date=17 August 2008 |work=BBC Sport |date=16 August 2008 |archive-date=14 January 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250114103849/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/olympics/swimming/7564653.stm |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Synchronised swimming==
{{See also|Synchronised swimming at the 2008 Summer Olympics}}
Team GB was represented by two artistic swimmers, [[Olivia Allison]] and [[Jenna Randall]], who placed 14th in the women's duet event. This was the first time since [[Synchronized swimming at the 1992 Summer Olympics|1992]] that Britain had taken part in the synchronised swimming competition at the Olympics.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.swimming.org/artistic-swimming/artistic-swimming-olympics/ |title=Artistic Swimming at the Olympics |website=Swim England |date=7 December 2016 |access-date=7 April 2025 |archive-date=12 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240412111241/https://www.swimming.org/artistic-swimming/artistic-swimming-olympics/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Taekwondo==
{{See also|Taekwondo at the 2008 Summer Olympics}}
Team GB entered three athletes into the taekwondo competition. [[Sarah Stevenson]] won Team GB's first-ever medal in [[Taekwondo at the Olympics|Olympic taekwondo]] – a bronze in the [[Taekwondo at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Women's +67 kg|women's +67&nbsp;kg]] category.<ref name="Taekwondo_medal">{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/olympics/taekwondo/7578208.stm|title=Reprieved Stevenson takes bronze|access-date=23 August 2008 |work=BBC Sport |date=23 August 2008 |archive-date=9 March 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170309090031/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/olympics/taekwondo/7578208.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> Another British hopeful, [[Aaron Cook (taekwondo)|Aaron Cook]], missed out on bronze in the [[Taekwondo at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Men's 80 kg|men's −80&nbsp;kg]], which led to his coach publicly criticising the referee's decisions.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2008/aug/22/olympics2008.olympicstaekwondo |title=Olympics: Cook misses out on medals as coach blasts referee |work=The Guardian |date=22 August 2008 |access-date=5 April 2025 |archive-date=11 February 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210211041430/https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2008/aug/22/olympics2008.olympicstaekwondo |url-status=live}}</ref>

==Tennis==
{{See also|Tennis at the 2008 Summer Olympics}}
Great Britain was represented in the tennis competition by brothers [[Andy Murray|Andy]] and [[Jamie Murray]]. In the first round of the singles tournament, Andy was defeated in straight sets by Chinese Taipei's [[Lu Yen-hsun]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2008/aug/11/olympics2008.olympicstennis1 |title=Olympics: Murray crashes out in first round of men's singles |work=The Guardian |last=Buckley |first=Will |date=11 August 2008 |access-date=12 April 2025 |archive-date=27 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230627033009/https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2008/aug/11/olympics2008.olympicstennis1 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/olympics/tennis/7553989.stm |title=Mixed Olympic fortunes for Murray |work=BBC Sport |date=11 August 2008 |access-date=12 April 2025 |archive-date=20 April 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200420011525/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/olympics/tennis/7553989.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> The Murray brothers were later eliminated in the second round of the men's doubles tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thetimes.com/travel/destinations/europe-travel/france/paris/andy-and-jamie-murray-crash-out-of-the-olympic-tennis-doubles-qxgvd8gx9dg |title=Andy and Jamie Murray crash out of the Olympic tennis doubles |work=The Times |date=13 August 2008 |access-date=12 April 2025 |archive-date=12 April 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250412111209/https://www.thetimes.com/travel/destinations/europe-travel/france/paris/andy-and-jamie-murray-crash-out-of-the-olympic-tennis-doubles-qxgvd8gx9dg |url-status=live |url-access=subscription }}</ref>

==Triathlon==
{{See also|Triathlon at the 2008 Summer Olympics}}
Five competitors were selected to represent Team GB in the triathlon, with three in the men's event and two in the women's.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://triathlon.org/news/british-olympic-team-confirmed1 |title=British Olympic Team Confirmed |website=[[triathlon.org]] |date=27 June 2008 |access-date=11 April 2025 |archive-date=11 April 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250411121157/https://triathlon.org/news/british-olympic-team-confirmed1 |url-status=live }}</ref> The best result was recorded by [[Alistair Brownlee]], who finished in 12th place.<ref name="olympics.com triathlon_men">{{cite web|url=https://www.olympics.com/en/olympic-games/beijing-2008/results/triathlon/individual-men |title=Beijing 2008, Triathlon Individual Men Results |website=olympics.com |access-date=11 April 2025 |archive-date=8 October 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241008201400/https://www.olympics.com/en/olympic-games/beijing-2008/results/triathlon/individual-men |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="olympics.com triathlon_women">{{cite web|url=https://www.olympics.com/en/olympic-games/beijing-2008/results/triathlon/individual-women |title=Beijing 2008, Triathlon Individual Women Results |website=olympics.com |access-date=11 April 2025 |archive-date=8 October 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241008201401/https://www.olympics.com/en/olympic-games/beijing-2008/results/triathlon/individual-women |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Weightlifting==
{{See also|Weightlifting at the 2008 Summer Olympics}}
The only British weightlifter to qualify for the Games was [[Michaela Breeze]] who was competing in her second Olympics.<ref>{{cite press release |url=http://www.olympics.org.uk/beijing2008/News.aspx?id=2493 |title=BOA Announces Weightlifting Member of Team GB |access-date=10 August 2008 |website=[[British Olympic Association|olympics.org.uk]] |date=15 July 2008 |archive-date=12 August 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080812203020/http://www.olympics.org.uk/beijing2008/News.aspx?id=2493 |url-status=dead }}</ref> She battled through a back injury, sustained less than a month before the Games,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.chinadaily.com.cn/olympics/2008-08/12/content_6929508.htm |title=British woman competes with injury at Olympics |work=[[China Daily]] |agency=[[Xinhua]] |date=12 August 2008 |access-date=16 May 2025 |archive-date=19 October 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191019040810/https://www.chinadaily.com.cn/olympics/2008-08/12/content_6929508.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> and finished 15th out of 20 competitors in her event.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/olympics/weightlifting/7555474.stm |title=Breeze performance hit by injury |access-date=20 August 2008 |work=[[BBC Sport]] |date=12 August 2008 |archive-date=6 March 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230306202515/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/olympics/weightlifting/7555474.stm |url-status=live }}</ref>
