==Sports not contested==
There was no Team GB representation at the 2008 Olympics in [[Baseball at the 2008 Summer Olympics|baseball]], [[Basketball at the 2008 Summer Olympics|basketball]], [[Football at the 2008 Summer Olympics|football]], [[Handball at the 2008 Summer Olympics|handball]], [[Softball at the 2008 Summer Olympics|softball]], [[Table tennis at the 2008 Summer Olympics|table tennis]], [[Volleyball at the 2008 Summer Olympics|volleyball]] and [[Wrestling at the 2008 Summer Olympics|wrestling]]. British athletes took part in the qualifying competitions for some of these sports in the lead up to the Games, but they either failed to qualify or were unable to participate for other reasons.<ref name="BBC_qual">{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/olympics/team_gb/7094118.stm |title=Team GB for Beijing / No GB Representation |work=BBC Sport |date=21 July 2008 |access-date=23 June 2025 |archive-date=13 March 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230313051325/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/olympics/team_gb/7094118.stm#nogb |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Baseball===
{{See also|Baseball at the 2008 Summer Olympics}}
The [[Great Britain national baseball team|GB baseball team]] finished second in the [[2007 European Baseball Championship]] behind [[Netherlands national baseball team|the Netherlands]], which guaranteed Britain a place at the Olympic qualifying tournament in [[Taiwan]]; however, a lack of funding forced the British team to withdraw (their place being taken by [[Germany national baseball team|Germany]]).<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/olympics/baseball/7279476.stm |title=GB's Olympic baseball dream ends |work=[[BBC Sport]] |date=5 March 2008 |access-date=17 September 2008 |last=Scrivener |first=Peter |archive-date=9 March 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080309010831/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/olympics/baseball/7279476.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> [[UK Sport]] had withdrawn funding for baseball after 2005, when the IOC [[Olympic sports#Changes since 2000|removed the sport from the Olympic program]] for the 2012 Games and beyond.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://nbcsports.msnbc.com/id/8504326/site/21683474/ |title=They'rrre out! Olympics drop baseball, softball |work=[[NBC Sports]] |agency=Associated Press |date=9 July 2005 |access-date=24 May 2025 |archive-date=12 August 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080812052814/http://nbcsports.msnbc.com/id/8504326/site/21683474/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Football===
{{See also|Football at the 2008 Summer Olympics}}
The award of the [[2012 Summer Olympics]] to London has brought the question of British participation in the football tournaments to the fore, given that there is traditionally no single [[United Kingdom national football team|United Kingdom national team]]. The [[British Olympic Association]] initially refused to rule out the possibility of entry for 2008, but were unable to come to an agreement with the [[Scottish Football Association]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Britain looks to Beijing after Scotland's snub to 2012 Games |url=https://www.thetimes.com/travel/destinations/uk-travel/scotland-travel/britain-looks-to-beijing-after-scotland-s-snub-to-2012-games-tk93b2q9mqk |work=The Times |date=12 November 2005 |access-date=30 March 2025 |location=London |first=John |last=Goodbody |archive-date=30 March 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250330065927/https://www.thetimes.com/travel/destinations/uk-travel/scotland-travel/britain-looks-to-beijing-after-scotland-s-snub-to-2012-games-tk93b2q9mqk |url-status=live }}</ref> The [[2007 UEFA European Under-21 Football Championship|2007 European Under-21 Championship]], which served as the European qualifying tournament for the men's competition, saw the [[England national under-21 football team|England U21 team]] reach the semi-finals, which would have meant a place at the Olympics. Because at the Olympics the team is representative of the entire UK, England were thus prevented from taking this place, with instead a play-off taking place between [[Portugal national under-21 football team|Portugal]] and [[Italy national under-21 football team|Italy]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=23 November 2006 |title=Finalists chase Olympic dream |url=https://www.uefa.com/under21/news/0257-0de67309de18-a8f66f8d4e5a-1000--finalists-chase-olympic-dream/ |access-date=24 September 2025 |website=UEFA.com |publisher=}}</ref><ref name="italy po">{{cite news |date=21 June 2007 |title=Soccer-Italy win Olympics place after Under-21 play-off |url=http://uk.reuters.com/article/soccer-under21-portugal-idUKL2123517520070621 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140302095157/http://uk.reuters.com/article/2007/06/21/soccer-under21-portugal-idUKL2123517520070621 |archive-date=2 March 2014 |access-date=24 September 2025 |agency=Reuters}}</ref> A similar situation occurred with the [[England women's national football team|England women's team]] who would have been granted a place at the 2008 Olympics by virtue of being one of the top three European sides at the [[2007 FIFA Women's World Cup|2007 World Cup]], but their Olympic qualification was disallowed by [[FIFA]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/women/6985988.stm |title=Olympic blow for England's women |date=9 September 2007|work=BBC Sport |access-date=25 May 2025 |archive-date=25 May 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250525152624/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/women/6985988.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> Instead, there was a play-off between [[Denmark women's national football team|Denmark]] and [[Sweden women's national football team|Sweden]] to claim the vacant Olympic qualifying position left by England.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/womensworldcup/news/01c6-0e10aed35fe7-3a39833e0010-1000--olympic-play-off-dates-set/ |title=Olympic play-off dates set |website=UEFA.com |date=10 October 2007 |access-date=25 May 2025 |archive-date=24 March 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250324035850/https://www.uefa.com/womensworldcup/news/01c6-0e10aed35fe7-3a39833e0010-1000--olympic-play-off-dates-set/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Media coverage==

As Britain's Olympic and Paralympic broadcaster,<ref name="BBC PR3">{{cite press release |title=The 2008 Beijing Olympics and Paralympics on the BBC – Olympics coverage on BBC TV |work=BBC Press Office |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/pressoffice/pressreleases/stories/2008/06_june/19/olympics3.shtml |date=19 June 2008 |access-date=20 May 2025 |archive-date=1 May 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250501100733/https://www.bbc.co.uk/pressoffice/pressreleases/stories/2008/06_june/19/olympics3.shtml |url-status=live }}</ref> the [[BBC]] held [[exclusive right]]s to [[Terrestrial television|terrestrial]] coverage of the 2008 Games in the United Kingdom,<ref name="Guardian.beijing2008.tvcoverage">{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/media/2008/aug/02/beijing2008.tvcoverage |title=So let the great wall-to-wall Games begin |last=Kelner |first=Martin |work=The Guardian |date=2 August 2008 |access-date=20 May 2025 |archive-date=16 September 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150916214559/https://www.theguardian.com/media/2008/aug/02/beijing2008.tvcoverage |url-status=live }}</ref> acquired under the [[Ofcom Code on Sports and Other Listed and Designated Events]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ofcom.org.uk/siteassets/resources/documents/tv-radio-and-on-demand/broadcast-codes/other-codes/ofcom_code_on_sport.pdf?v=331621 |title=Code on Sports and Other Listed and Designated Events |website=[[Ofcom|Ofcom.org.uk]] |access-date=20 May 2025 |archive-date=15 July 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240715233005/https://www.ofcom.org.uk/siteassets/resources/documents/tv-radio-and-on-demand/broadcast-codes/other-codes/ofcom_code_on_sport.pdf?v=331621 |url-status=live }}</ref> An extensive range of broadcasting options was employed to provide over 2,750 hours of TV coverage.<ref name="BBC">{{cite press release |title=The 2008 Beijing Olympics and Paralympics on the BBC – The Beijing Games on the BBC |work=BBC Press Office |date=19 June 2008 |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/pressoffice/pressreleases/stories/2008/06_june/19/olympics.shtml |access-date=20 June 2008 |archive-date=1 May 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250501115421/https://www.bbc.co.uk/pressoffice/pressreleases/stories/2008/06_june/19/olympics.shtml |url-status=live }}</ref>

For the first time, Olympic coverage was broadcast in [[high-definition television|high definition]] on the [[BBC HD]] channel.<ref name="BBC" /> [[Digital TV]] viewers had access to up to six streamed channels covering the Games on [[BBC Red Button]], whilst the [[BBC Online|BBC's website]] permitted British broadband users to view live streams from a variety of events.<ref name="BBC 7102062">{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/olympics/7102062.stm |title=Beijing Olympics on the BBC |work=BBC Sport |date=30 July 2008 |access-date=15 May 2025 |archive-date=29 January 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250129035325/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/olympics/7102062.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> Live broadcasts ran overnight and throughout the day on [[BBC One]] and [[BBC Two]], starting at 02:00 daily; a highlights programme, ''The Games Today'',<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/b00cmjqr |title=The Games Today, Beijing 2008 – Daily round-up of action from the Beijing Olympics |website=BBC One |access-date=15 May 2025}}</ref> was broadcast on BBC One following the close of each day's events.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/olympics/2522307/Beijing-Olympics-2008-TV-viewing-guide.html |title=Beijing Olympics 2008: TV viewing guide |last=Ruddick |first=Graham |work=The Telegraph |date=7 August 2008 |access-date=15 May 2025 |archive-date=11 October 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191011105713/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/olympics/2522307/Beijing-Olympics-2008-TV-viewing-guide.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

The opening and closing ceremonies were anchored by [[Sue Barker]] and [[Huw Edwards (journalist)|Huw Edwards]], with additional commentary from [[Hazel Irvine]] and [[Carrie Gracie]].<ref name="BBC" /><ref name="BBC PR5" /> For the duration of the Games, general coverage was delivered at various times of the day by a large team of BBC presenters,<ref name="Guardian.beijing2008.tvcoverage" /> including Barker, Irvine, [[Adrian Chiles]], [[Clare Balding]], [[Gabby Logan]], [[Jake Humphrey]], and [[John Inverdale]].<ref name="BBC" /> Detailed analysis was provided by a selection of former Olympic contenders, including gold medallists [[Michael Johnson (athlete)|Michael Johnson]] (athletics), [[Jonathan Edwards (triple jumper)|Jonathan Edwards]] (athletics), [[Shirley Robertson]] (sailing), [[Adrian Moorhouse]] (swimming), [[Sir Steve Redgrave]] (rowing), and [[Chris Boardman]] (cycling).<ref name="BBC PR5">{{cite press release |title=The 2008 Beijing Olympics and Paralympics on the BBC – The BBC television team |work=BBC Press Office |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/pressoffice/pressreleases/stories/2008/06_june/19/olympics5.shtml |date=19 June 2008 |access-date=22 September 2008 |archive-date=1 May 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250501225116/https://www.bbc.co.uk/pressoffice/pressreleases/stories/2008/06_june/19/olympics5.shtml |url-status=live }}</ref>

[[Eurosport]] provided continuous [[pay-TV]] coverage of the 2008 Games across its territories, viewable in the UK to [[Sky UK|Sky TV]] subscribers, including 15&nbsp;hours a day of live broadcasting between 03:00 and 18:00.<ref>{{cite press release |title=Eurosport Unveils Beijing 2008 Programming |website=Sportcal.com |date=16 June 2008 |url=http://www.sportcal.com/News/release_article.aspx?articleID=60690&kind=press |access-date=20 June 2008 |archive-date=19 February 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120219071303/http://www.sportcal.com/News/release_article.aspx?articleID=60690&kind=press |url-status=dead}}</ref> The coverage was also available in high definition on Eurosport's new HD channel (first launched in July 2008) to the thousands of [[Sky+ HD]] subscribers across the UK.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://uk.themedialeader.com/eurosport-launches-high-definition/ |title=Eurosport Launches High Definition |website=The Media Leader |date=16 July 2008 |access-date=23 May 2025 |archive-date=23 May 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250523165904/https://uk.themedialeader.com/eurosport-launches-high-definition/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Eurosport's Olympic broadcast sponsor for 2008 was the sportswear brand [[Asics]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.campaignlive.co.uk/article/asics-sponsor-eurosports-beijing-olympics-coverage/778068 |title=Asics to sponsor Eurosport's Beijing Olympics coverage |last=Kemp |first=Ed |website=[[Campaign (magazine)|Campaign]] |date=21 January 2008 |access-date=23 May 2025 |archive-date=23 May 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250523170404/https://www.campaignlive.co.uk/article/asics-sponsor-eurosports-beijing-olympics-coverage/778068 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Radio coverage was provided by [[BBC Radio 5 Live]], and [[BBC Radio 5 Live Sports Extra]] on [[Digital Audio Broadcasting|digital radio]].<ref name="BBC" />
